sentences.text: Delano Valentim de Andrade is chief executive officer of BB Seguridade Participacoes, the insurance holding controlled by Banco do Brasil.

The board elected him diretor-presidente on August 12, 2025 for the 2025-2027 term, with his investiture set for August 20 of that year, succeeding Andre Haui, who had led the company since February 2024.

sentences.quote: the company's capital-light structure, which outsources most underwriting risk to its operating subsidiaries, allows it to sustain high payout ratios without jeopardising regulatory solvency buffers
sentences.text: BB Seguridade, the insurance, pension and premium bonds holding controlled by Banco do Brasil, runs a capital-light model in which underwriting sits at operating subsidiaries, supporting high payouts without straining solvency buffers.

sentences.quote: Analysts noted that the company's capital-light structure, which outsources most underwriting risk to its operating subsidiaries, allows it to sustain high payout ratios without jeopardising regulatory solvency buffers.
sentences.text: Analysts note this structure allows it to sustain high payout ratios without jeopardising regulatory solvency.

sentences.quote: The board approved an interim dividend of R$3.85 billion (US$757.5 million), equivalent to R$1.9833 (US$0.39) per share.
sentences.text: Shareholder returns are the core of the case: the company paid 3.9 billion reais in dividends, an 88% payout ratio, with a remuneration policy distributing at least 70 percent of annual net profit.
Pensions are the growth engine, as Brasilprev reserves reached 496.5 billion reais, a record for the business.
High Brazilian interest rates lift financial income, with net investment income after taxes up 16% in the first half.
Earnings have stayed resilient: recurring net managerial income reached 4.4 billion reais in H1 2026, up 3.2% year over year, though crop insurance remains the main weak spot.

thesis_pillars.text: BB Seguridade, the insurance, pension and premium bonds holding controlled by Banco do Brasil, runs a capital-light model in which underwriting sits at operating subsidiaries, supporting high payouts without straining solvency buffers. Analysts note this structure allows it to sustain high payout ratios without jeopardising regulatory solvency.
